key_insight: BenchX introduces a large-scale benchmark to measure how well cancer detection and localization models hold up across different patient demographics and imaging protocols. The key takeaway is that strong average performance can hide major biases and failure modes in real clinical settings.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the lack of a standardized, large-scale way to evaluate AI models for cancer detection and localization under demographic differences and protocol variation, such as age, sex, and contrast phase changes.
method: Build an open benchmark dataset of 85,355 medical imaging cases for cancer detection and localization.
Evaluate AI models across demographic groups and imaging protocol conditions to expose performance gaps.
Compare model behavior on challenging scenarios such as small tumors and scans from different contrast phases.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, BenchX provides a practical framework for testing robustness, fairness, and clinical reliability before deployment. It helps identify hidden bias and failure modes that may not appear in standard aggregate metrics.
visual_elements: Benchmark pipeline diagram showing data collection, grouping by demographics/protocols, and model evaluation
Grouped bar chart comparing performance across age, sex, and contrast phase categories
Heatmap highlighting model failure rates for small tumors and other hard cases
Icon set representing demographics, scan protocols, and localization targets
paper_title: BenchX: Benchmarking AI Models for Cancer Detection and Localization with Demographic and Protocol Biases
paper_authors: Qi Chen, Wenxuan Li, Pedro R. A. S. Bassi, Xinze Zhou, Jakob Wasserthal
